answer: Require each agent to lock a stake in a time-locked vault that thaws as slowly as a glacier: the deposit vests over weeks, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets ties up real capital for a long time. To keep the stake active, the agent must emit a regular pulse - a signed heartbeat proving it still controls its keys and is doing useful work. Missed pulses slash the stake, and early withdrawal forfeits it. Sybils become expensive to create and costly to maintain, while honest agents pay only patience.
